The HEAT toolkit addresses stakeholder engagement by guiding users through the process of consulting and including diverse stakeholders in the design process. It emphasizes the importance of engaging different stakeholders, particularly marginalized and vulnerable groups, to identify both intended and unintended consequences of AI systems. The toolkit provides instructions on how to identify relevant stakeholders and encourages meaningful and power-sensitive engagement, while also addressing potential issues like tokenism and participation-washing.

In terms of environmental sustainability, HEAT includes a section dedicated to assessing and mitigating the environmental impact of AI systems. It introduces methods for calculating the carbon footprint of AI models and conducting Life Cycle Analysis. The toolkit encourages users to rethink their product design with environmental considerations in mind, promoting more-than-human-centered design practices that acknowledge the interconnectedness of all living things and aim to align human goals with non-human needs and environmental constraints.
